title: Thermomix Beef Chuck Ragù
description: Slow-braised chuck with a single star anise for depth. Seared in cast iron, braised in the Thermomix. Better the next day.

steps.text: Pat the chuck ({{beef}}) completely dry and season with the salt ({{salt}}) and pepper ({{pepper}}). Sear in a hot cast iron pan with half the olive oil ({{oil*0.5}}), in two or three batches, until each side is properly dark. Do not crowd the pan. Set aside with any resting juices.
Onion ({{onion}}), carrot ({{carrot}}), celery ({{celery}} stalks) and garlic ({{garlic}} cloves) into the bowl. Chop 5 sec / Speed 5. Scrape down.
Add the remaining olive oil ({{oil*0.5}}). Sauté 5 min / 120°C / Speed 1, until softened and fragrant.
Add the tomato paste ({{tomato-paste}}). Cook 2 min / 120°C / Reverse / Speed 1 to take the raw edge off it.
Pour the red wine ({{wine}}) into the hot cast iron and scrape up the fond, then tip it into the bowl. Cook 5 min / 120°C / Reverse / Speed 1, MC off, to reduce by about half.
Add the tomatoes ({{tomatoes}}), stock ({{stock}}), bay leaf ({{bay}}) and star anise ({{star-anise}}). Return the beef and its juices. Do not fill past the 2L mark.
Cook 90 min / 98°C / Reverse / Soft stir, MC on. On a TM6, Slow Cook mode for 90 minutes to 2 hours also works. Check at 80 minutes: the beef should give way under a fork.
Remove the star anise and bay leaf before you shred. Left in through the shredding, the anise stops being background and starts tasting like five spice.
Shred 5–10 sec / Reverse / Speed 3, checking as you go. If the sauce is loose, cook 10 min / Varoma / Reverse / Soft stir, MC off, to tighten it. Taste and adjust the salt.
Cook the pasta ({{pasta}}) a minute short of the packet time. Drain, reserving a cup of the water, and toss through the ragù with a splash of it until it clings.

notes.title: Confidence
notes.text: The braise structure and the single star anise are sourced (Blumenthal adds one to Hazan's method). The 90-minute timing is my estimate for 4cm chuck cubes, so check at 80 minutes. Not confirmed whether a TM5 accepts a single 90-minute timer; if it caps at 60, run it twice.

notes.title: Capacity
notes.text: Do not scale past 4 serves in the bowl. 800g of beef with the sauce is already close to the limit.

notes.title: 1kg of beef
notes.text: Too much for one Thermomix batch. Sear in the cast iron and finish in a covered dish in the oven at 150°C for 2.5–3 hours, then freeze half the finished sauce. That version has not been written up as its own card yet.

notes.title: How long is too long
notes.text: Sweet spot is about 90 minutes to 2 hours in the Thermomix, 2.5–3 hours in the oven at 150°C. Past that the beef dries and the tomato goes flat, and in the Thermomix the blade turns the meat to paste. To go longer, use the oven at 130°C.

notes.title: Frozen beef
notes.text: Cold water thaw in a sealed bag, about 30 minutes per 500g, changing the water every 30 minutes. Pat very dry before searing; frozen or wet beef steams rather than browns.

notes.title: Further upgrades, not on this card
notes.text: Sourced options for next time: a parmesan rind in the simmering basket, 2–3 anchovies melted into the soffritto, a tablespoon of cold butter stirred through at the end, or a 50/50 split of shin and chuck.
